claims.summary: astrid:llm scans bytes for known control markers and distinguishes markers merely present from markers used as grammatical subject; scan_known_model_control_markers (L114) rebuilds `remainder` preserving a marker only when it has valid reference_syntax (L129-130).
claims.disposition: Verified against complete source at SHA 902a0358. reference_syntax (L49-60) returns Some only when the marker is delimiter-wrapped OR followed by an explicit relation verb; L129 pushes occurrence.token to remainder only if reference_syntax.is_some(). Accurate observation.

claims.summary: Snag 1: first_word_after (L89) uses split_whitespace + char filter, so a colon/complex phrase (e.g. "X: acts as Y") might make it fail to identify "acts" as the relation verb.
claims.disposition: Mechanism contradicted by source and already regressed. L89-96 trim_matches strips non-alnum/underscore boundary chars and split_whitespace separates the colon, so first_word_after returns "acts" regardless of leading punctuation. Live regression control_marker_cleanup_first_word_after_skips_leading_punctuation_transition (tests.rs:2635) proves this across `--`. A marker before "acts" drops because "acts" is unlisted (L64-86), not because extraction fails.

claims.summary: Snag 2: saturating_add(character.len_utf8()) (L138-139) is safe and the logic treats any character not starting a known marker as a single-character unit pushed to remainder.
claims.disposition: Verified at source L133-140. The else-branch takes exactly one char via chars().next(), pushes it to remainder, and advances offset by len_utf8() through saturating_add. Accurate; no overflow path.

claims.summary: Test 1: verify exact_reference_delimiter_syntax (L199) identifies nested/complex delimiters like `「...」` or `⟦...⟧` and returns Some when surrounding chars match allowed pairs.
claims.disposition: Verified: both pairs are in exact_reference_delimiter_pair (「」 L168 -> QuotedExactKnownToken; ⟦⟧ L180 -> GroupedExactKnownToken). Already regressed: ⟦...⟧ in control_marker_cleanup_preserves_bounded_nested_delimiter_stacks (tests.rs:2179); 「...」 in control_marker_cleanup_preserves_quoted_exact_tokens_across_whitespace (tests.rs:2404). No new test warranted.

claims.summary: Test 2: assert a marker followed by "is a tool" is EXCLUDED from remainder because "is a" does not match allowed verbs in followed_by_explicit_exact_token_relation (L64).
claims.disposition: Contradiction, preserved not domesticated. followed_by_explicit_exact_token_relation (L64) checks only first_word_after = "is", which IS allowlisted (L76), so the marker is PRESERVED, not excluded. Her expected exclusion is incorrect (same class as prior 1786319270 correction). Correct behavior already regressed: control_marker_cleanup_distinguishes_allowlisted_is_from_unlisted_acts (tests.rs:2568) uses the exact "is a substitute for" phrase and asserts first_word_after=="is" + preservation. Her underlying concern (present-vs-subject boundary, multi-word relations) is real and captured.
